work.text: Confidential GPU capacity. A miner runs a Kubernetes cluster of 8-GPU worker nodes with Intel TDX and NVIDIA confidential computing, posts a 100 TAO deposit on its own hotkey, and is onboarded by hand. What is paid for today is capacity that passes a readiness check, priced per GPU-hour; job execution and attestation are not yet scored.
work.quote: miners earn Bittensor emissions for providing confidential compute capacity and reliably executing Armada-scheduled jobs

scoring.text: A dollar target, not a benchmark. Each cycle the validator reads every miner cluster through Rancher, passes or fails a binary readiness verdict (hotkey binding, high-availability topology, 8-GPU workers, GPU passthrough, runtime handler), and for each ready miner computes GPU count times the card price per GPU-hour times tenure times window hours. Tenure is fixed at 1.0 while the reliability gate is unwired.
scoring.quote: usd_target_per_hour x tenure x window_hours / usd_per_alpha; tenure: float = 1.0  # 0..1: 1.0 while the reliability gate is not wired
scoring.disagrees: The README's economics section says emissions are weighted by attested TEE health, job-execution quality and uptime and that no attestation means no emissions; its What Ships Today table and the code at the pinned commit put only Rancher readiness in the weight path, with attestation, Armada metrics and health designed and not yet scored.

split.text: Proportional to dollar target, capped by the pool. Each ready miner's earned dollars over the epoch's emission pool in dollars is its weight; the remainder is set on the owner UID, which under recycle returns the alpha to unissued supply. On 2026-09-20 the dashboard showed two clusters: the owner's staging cluster UID 56 at 64 percent of the pool and BTLABS UID 97 at 32 percent, $31.48 recycled.
split.quote: Whatever miners do not earn is recycled to the owner UID (set as weight on the owner's hotkey). Weights are normalized to sum 1.0.

judges.text: Six validators were active on the 2026-09-09 chain snapshot. Commit-reveal is on; weights may be set once per 100 blocks. The validator reads cluster inventory through a GET-only Rancher client, TAO/USD from Taostats, and Targon's payout feed to clamp the price card downward; the subnet-owner validator publishes the price snapshot and dashboard to Hippius. A cycle without a trustworthy price, inventory or metagraph read is skipped.
judges.quote: commit_reveal_weights_enabled True, weights_rate_limit 100, yuma_version 3; chain-2026-09-09.json active_validators 6

cadence.text: Emission settles every 360 blocks, about 72 minutes. The README says the validator sets weights once per epoch, boundary-aligned; the config's window is one hour by default, so a miner earns its hourly target per cycle. The Hippius dashboard on 2026-09-20 read epoch 25,293. A new registration is immune from deregistration for 5,000 blocks, about 16 hours.

buyer.text: Not an enterprise yet. The only recorded income is idle GPU capacity sold as confidential inference of GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash and Ornith-1.5-397B through sayGM, subnet 28, with the alpha earned swapped to SN90 and recycled daily. The validator's card prices GPU-hours from $2.00 for an RTX 6000 to $9.75 for a B300; paid jobs in TAO or alpha are a Phase 2 item.
buyer.quote: KubeTEE serves inference on sayGM (Bittensor SN28). The alpha earned is swapped to SN90 and recycled

exploits.text: No incident is recorded. With one production miner and the owner's staging cluster, the guardrails are structural: the GPU card is clamped downward to what Targon pays per card, floored at 75 percent of the card; a miner absent for sustained cycles is deregistered under a guard; the 100 TAO deposit is measured, not enforced; a cycle without a trustworthy price or inventory read keeps the previous weights.
exploits.quote: A cycle that cannot get a trustworthy price, Rancher inventory, or metagraph read is skipped rather than guessed
